citations.claim: Quidra is described in its own README as a statically typed, native general-purpose programming language designed for both humans and language models.
Official release pages show the canonical repository has zero stars and zero forks.
No independent Quidra Stack Overflow, forum, or blog presence was found in the queries executed.

metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.limitations: Search-engine-index-based sampling can under-count very recent or low-SEO-visibility discussion (e.g., private Discord/Slack communities, non-indexed forum posts). Raw indicators such as GitHub star/fork counts were used only as declared supplementary evidence alongside the search-absence findings, not as a standalone proxy, per ecosystem.md guidance on raw popularity indicators. Search budget for this task was capped at 5 provider-backed queries; all were used on this single requirement given the single assigned language.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.methodology: Predeclared sampling per ecosystem.md: assessed whether independent, externally observable community/public knowledge sources exist for Quidra (Q&A sites, forums, blogs/tutorials, third-party write-ups) beyond the language's own maintained repository/documentation. Same retrieval depth (multiple targeted web searches) applied as would be applied to any other assigned language in this evaluation family.
raw_findings: Quidra's only discoverable public presence across all four queries is the official GitHub organization repository quidra-lang/quidra and its releases/pull-request pages.
GitHub release pages for v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 explicitly show 'Fork 0 · Star 0', indicating no external community engagement signal on the canonical repository at the time of retrieval.
No Stack Overflow tag, question, or answer mentioning Quidra (the language) was found; the Stack Overflow-focused query surfaced only unrelated general Stack Overflow statistics pages.

No Reddit thread, independent forum, third-party blog post, or tutorial about the Quidra language was found; the reddit/forum/blog query surfaced only unrelated results (a generic 'how to use Reddit' guide, an unrelated 'Lang-8' language-exchange site, an unrelated company named 'Quid Inc.', and an unrelated conlang site 'Langmaker').

All substantive Quidra-specific content found originates from the project's own repository: README description, release notes, and internal pull requests/issues authored by the project's own contributors (e.g., koba-jon) rather than by an independent third-party community.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.retrieval_route: Provider-backed web_search tool, 4 queries executed: 'Quidra programming language'; '"Quidra" language Stack Overflow quidra-lang'; '"quidra-lang" reddit OR forum OR blog OR tutorial'; 'quidra-lang stackoverflow tag questions'.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.score_derivation: Rubric treats absence of independently observable community/public knowledge (no Q&A tag activity, no third-party tutorials/blogs, no forum discussion, negligible repo social signal) as the rubric-defined low end of the 0-100 scale rather than N/A, per ecosystem.md ('Unsupported or absent ecosystem evidence intentionally covered by a metric receives the rubric-defined low score rather than N/A'). Quidra shows: (a) one official maintained repository with essentially no external stars/forks/engagement, (b) zero located Stack Overflow tag/question presence, (c) zero located independent forum/Reddit/blog/tutorial coverage. This is consistent with a benchmark-target/very-new language with no established public community footprint. Score set to 3/100: not 0 because the project does have a public GitHub repository with structured documentation and versioned releases (a minimal, self-published public knowledge surface), but far below any language with genuine third-party community knowledge (Q&A ecosystem, tutorials, forum discussion).
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.selection_rule: Frozen query set decided before evidence collection: (1) general language-name search to locate canonical public identity/repo, (2) Stack Overflow tag/question search, (3) Reddit/forum/blog/tutorial search, (4) direct 'stackoverflow tag questions' search for the project's GitHub org name. Candidate universe = general web search index reachable via the search tool; no cherry-picking of first hits, all returned domains considered.
